title: SecB Failure Evidence Envelope (WP1 deliverable 1)
description: Formalizes SECB-FAIL-LEARN-001 section 6 as strict JSON Schema. Supersedes-in-design (not yet effective; requires REV+SEC and Human GOV) the informal v0.1 docs/templates/failure-evidence-envelope.yaml. LIMITATIONS the schema layer cannot close, all deferred to semantic-validator.mjs or to WP2+ runtime: (1) recomputing the content-address digest to detect tampering (validateContentAddressIntegrity) -- SCEN-04; (2) proving affected_resources/mutation_committed matches what ACTUALLY happened at runtime rather than what the record claims -- WP2 capture-time concern; (3) literal secret-content scanning of free-text fields -- this schema forbids the SHAPE of secret-carrying fields (additionalProperties:false everywhere, sanitized_message pattern-forbids common secret-shaped substrings, contains_secrets is hard-const-false) but cannot prove a secret was never embedded inside an otherwise-innocuous string; real secret scanning is a WP2 capture-time control (section 8's 'redaction before durable serialization').

evidence_id.description: Content-addressed id: 'fev_' + sha256 hex of the canonical envelope with evidence_id and governance.integrity_signature excluded. See semantic-validator.mjs validateContentAddressIntegrity.

successor_of.description: When present, this envelope is a linked correction of a prior sealed envelope (section 6: 'Corrections SHALL create a linked successor'). Sealed evidence is never edited in place.

sanitized_message.description: Structural (not semantic) secret guard: forbids common secret-shaped substrings. This is a best-effort schema-layer defense, not a substitute for the WP2 redaction/secret-scan control. Hardened in rework round 02 (SEC-FL-WP1-002) to match keyword trigger words case-insensitively (e.g. 'API_KEY:' is now caught, not just 'api_key='). STILL-DEFERRED, NOT fixed by this hardening (would require real entropy-based secret detection, out of WP1 schema-pattern reach): (1) a keyword with a non-standard separator or spacing, e.g. 'the secret_key is abcdef...' with no '=' or ':' immediately after the keyword; (2) a bare high-entropy secret (AWS key, JWT, etc.) with no trigger keyword nearby at all. See governance.redaction_attestation for the companion contract-level attestation hook that names this gap explicitly rather than leaving it contract-silent.

stacktrace_reference.description: Must be an encrypted-object reference, never raw stack text (section 6: 'stacktrace_reference: encrypted-object-reference').

contains_secrets.description: Hard requirement, section 14: secrets SHALL never enter evidence. Always false; there is no allowed path for an admissible envelope to declare true.

redaction_attestation.description: Added rework round 02 (SEC-FL-WP1-002). See common.schema.json#/$defs/redaction_attestation for the full limitation note. Enforced here: an envelope cannot be marked admissible while its own redaction_attestation.redaction_applied is false (see this schema's allOf) -- this closes the 'contract-silent' gap without claiming real secret-content verification.

allOf.description: SCEN-02 / matrix row 1: a denied action produces evidence WITHOUT performing the action -- denial implies no committed mutation and no affected resources.

SCEN-01: fail-closed application must be evidenced whenever the result is denied or failed -- an unauthorized-operation record cannot claim fail_closed_applied=false while also reporting the operation as denied/failed.
If no mutation was committed there can be no affected resources to report, independent of decision.result (covers cancelled/timed_out/partially_completed cases with mutation_committed=false too).

Rework round 02 (SEC-FL-WP1-002): an envelope cannot be marked admissible while confessing no redaction step was ever claimed to run. This does NOT prove a secret is absent (see redaction_attestation's own description) -- it only closes the narrower, WP1-appropriate gap that an admissible record could omit the claim entirely.
